exposure: mothers with two or three or more previous pregnancies
mothers without any live children or one live child at birth
deliveries took place in public/university hospitals or philanthropic hospitals
cohort: The study included 931 cases and 1,862 controls of live births in Cuiaba, State of Mato Grosso, Brazil, from January 2015 to December 2018.
finding: The study found that higher maternal parity, fewer live children, multiple pregnancy, inadequate prenatal care, delivery in public/philanthropic hospitals, non-cephalic presentation, and uninduced labor were associated with an increased risk of neonatal near-miss.
mod_finding: Factors related to the birth process, specifically non-cephalic presentation and uninduced labor, were associated with an increased risk of neonatal near-miss.
